mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a demand surge.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and compresses valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect is not statistically significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a broader economic downturn.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages signals a labor market expansion with slack, which boosts consumption and corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market expansion with slack regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during wage inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in Real Gross Domestic Product (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly change < 0% for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during supply-side shocks.
